graph_edits.rationale: Align the courtyard/void logic to the verified access side so the public threshold becomes legible at the frontage.
Propagate the access-aligned opening through the first courtyard step to strengthen public ground response.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant mass with a stepped/canted upper body and a carved roof void, so it avoids fragmentation and holds together across the four views. The main weakness is access/publicness: the blue frontage edge is not answered by a strongly legible ground threshold, court, or undercut, so the void logic feels internal rather than openly civic. Still, the mass plausibly supports neighborhood living/commercial edge conditions better than a generic box because it has a clear hierarchy, a compact occupied volume, and some carved open-space figure. It does not collapse into a pure stair-step cliché; the section is more like a single compressed mass with a roof court. The references reinforce that a compact street building with a sheltered interior void and active frontage is the right precedent family, while the tower and bridge images are only partial principle transfers.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact street-facing commercial mass with a clear carved/open interior court and calibrated upper enclosure.
Soft public room logic: perimeter enclosure around a sheltered void, with strong indoor-outdoor threshold.
Small neighborhood frontage with legible threshold and concentrated service/body relationship.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Tower typology is much larger and more vertical than this candidate; use only the ground/public-edge principle.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Active ground and stacked hierarchy are useful, but the high-rise typology is only partially transferable.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual office/bridge typology is not program-matched; avoid copying the overall building form.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Long-span bridge-like continuity can inform connector/public-threshold thinking.

warnings: Frontage response is under-articulated relative to the verified access edge; consider opening a side or carving a clearer entry seam on the access-facing side.
Void is present but not yet convincingly public at ground level.
The silhouette is coherent, but the upper stepping could be simplified if later variants become too tiered.
